For retailers, building customer loyalty can therefore involve more than offering products at competitive prices. It also requires businesses to understand what customers value and create experiences that encourage them to return.
Technology is also becoming increasingly important in how retailers build these customer relationships.
Retailers are leveraging artificial intelligence (AI), unified commerce and customer data to create more connected shopping journeys across online and physical channels.
These tools allow businesses to meet customers wherever they are, while making interactions more consistent and personalised.
Customer data can also provide retailers with insights beyond who is making a purchase. It can help brands understand customer behaviour and identify who may be more likely to return.
The shift means that technologies once associated primarily with larger enterprises are increasingly becoming accessible to smaller businesses.
For SMEs, AI, customer data and unified commerce are becoming part of the infrastructure needed to build sustainable retail operations.
Retail Summit Asia was designed as a platform for retailers, founders and industry leaders to exchange practical insights and real business experiences.
Rather than focusing solely on short-term growth, the summit explored how businesses can develop the relationships, technology and infrastructure needed to remain competitive as the retail landscape changes.
The event was supported by AFFIN as Marquee Partner, alongside Fiuu and J&T Express as Strategic Partners.
Their solutions supported different aspects of the retail ecosystem, including payments, logistics and in-store experiences.
Ultimately, the discussions at Retail Summit Asia 2026 highlighted that building a retail business that lasts requires more than attracting the next customer. It involves understanding existing customers, strengthening their experience and putting the right technology and infrastructure in place to support long-term growth.

title: Malaysia Marks 10 Years at Tokyo Game Show as Homegrown Studios Target Global Gaming Market
bodyText:
Malaysia is marking a decade of participation at Tokyo Game Show (TGS) as five homegrown game studios showcase their original intellectual properties (IPs) and creative capabilities at the 2026 edition of the global gaming event.
Taking place from 17 to 21 September 2026 at Makuhari Messe, Chiba, Japan, TGS 2026 brings together major players from across the global games ecosystem, including publishers, investors, platform owners, distributors, developers and other industry stakeholders.
The Malaysia Pavilion is jointly organised by the Malaysia External Trade Development Corporation (MATRADE) and Malaysia Digital Economy Corporation (MDEC).
This year’s participating Malaysian companies are Algoin Tech, Fuloso, Magnus Games Studio, Metropolice and Vmagery Studio, representing a range of capabilities across game development, original IP creation, 2D and 3D game art and animation, as well as cinematic and immersive digital solutions.
The 2026 participation marks 10 years of Malaysia’s presence at Tokyo Game Show, providing a platform for local studios to showcase their creative and technical capabilities while building connections with international industry players.
The Malaysia Pavilion will facilitate business engagements through a curated programme that includes business matching sessions with strategic partners.
These engagements are intended to open opportunities for Malaysian companies in areas including publishing, licensing, co-development, investment and other commercial partnerships.
MATRADE Chief Executive Officer Dato’ Indera Abu Bakar Yusof said the decade-long participation reflects Malaysia’s growing capabilities and ambitions in the global digital creative and gaming industry.
“Our 10-year participation at Tokyo Game Show is a testament to Malaysia’s growing strength and ambition in the global digital creative and gaming industry. Malaysian studios are not only simply showcasing their capabilities, but they are also creating original intellectual properties, building international partnerships and delivering globally competitive creative solutions,” he said. “MATRADE has facilitated the participation of more than 60 Malaysian companies at TGS over the past years, generating export opportunities worth RM1.31 billion. MATRADE will continue to leverage strategic platforms such as TGS to accelerate the internationalisation of Malaysian companies and translate our creative strengths into sustainable export opportunities,” he added.
The five participating studios represent the breadth of Malaysia’s growing digital creative ecosystem.
Their offerings include original games and IPs inspired by Malaysia’s cultural heritage, alongside specialised services in 2D and 3D game art, animation, cinematic production and immersive digital solutions.
The emphasis on original intellectual property also highlights the growing role of Malaysian companies not only as service providers, but as creators of their own games and creative content for international audiences.
MDEC Chief Executive Officer Anuar Fariz Fadzil said Malaysia’s game development ecosystem continues to develop through its pool of creative talent, technical capabilities and original IPs.
“Malaysia’s game development ecosystem continues to grow, supported by a strong pool of creative talent, sophisticated capabilities and original IPs with international appeal. TGS offers our studios an opportunity to showcase their creativity and technical expertise while building meaningful connections with global industry players. MDEC remains committed to supporting Malaysian talent and companies in expanding their presence in international markets,” he said.
Beyond showcasing games, Tokyo Game Show provides Malaysian companies with access to potential international business partners across the gaming value chain.
Publishers, investors, platform owners, distributors and developers attending the event create opportunities for participating studios to explore new commercial relationships and expand their international networks.
For Malaysia, these engagements form part of a broader effort to internationalise local digital creative companies and convert domestic creative capabilities into export opportunities.
MATRADE said it has facilitated the participation of more than 60 Malaysian companies at Tokyo Game Show over the years, generating export opportunities valued at RM1.31 billion.
Malaysia is home to more than 300 animation and game development studios, supported by a skilled and multilingual talent pool with strong technical capabilities.
The country’s digital creative sector generates more than RM5 billion annually through exports, outsourcing, original IP development and digital content production.
This growing ecosystem positions Malaysia as a destination for global companies seeking creative and digital services while providing local studios with opportunities to expand into international markets.
With Malaysian game studios continuing to develop original IPs and build international partnerships, platforms such as Tokyo Game Show remain an important avenue for connecting the country’s creative capabilities with the wider global gaming industry.

title: Rolls-Royce Unveils Phantom Hummingbird with First-Ever Abalone Shell Marquetry
bodyText:
Rolls-Royce Motor Cars has unveiled Phantom Hummingbird, a Phantom Extended Private Commission featuring the marque’s first-ever use of abalone shell marquetry in a motor car.
Commissioned as a private tribute to the client’s wife and curated through Private Office Dubai, the Bespoke creation takes inspiration from the hummingbird, a symbol of joy, resilience and the ability to find beauty in every moment.
The design celebrates the intricate beauty of the natural world through the use of abalone shell and mother-of-pearl, chosen for their natural iridescence and ability to reflect changing colours in the light.
“The natural world has always been a rich source of inspiration for Rolls-Royce Bespoke commissions, offering extraordinary forms and colours for our designers and craftspeople to interpret. Our clients continually invite us to explore that inspiration in new and unexpected ways, as this remarkable Private Commission so perfectly demonstrates. The introduction of abalone shell into Rolls-Royce marquetry presented our designers and craftspeople with a fresh creative and technical challenge, resulting in an elegant tribute to the hummingbird’s mesmerising presence,” said Phil Fabre de la Grange, Head of Bespoke, Rolls-Royce Motor Cars.
At the heart of Phantom Hummingbird is the pioneering use of abalone shell, prized for its extraordinary natural iridescence.
The nacreous inner surface of the shell produces a distinctive blue-green lustre as it interacts with light. Combined with mother-of-pearl, the material is used to recreate the shimmering feathers of a hummingbird.
The choice of material reflects the natural way in which a hummingbird’s plumage changes colour. Its vivid hues are created by microscopic structures within the feathers that split and reflect light, producing flashes of colour that shift depending on the viewing angle.
The natural theme extends to the exterior, where a hand-painted hummingbird completes the Coachline.
The intricate marquetry is spread across three interior panels, with a hummingbird taking flight on each of the two Picnic Tables and a botanical composition appearing on the Rear Waterfall panel between the rear seats.
Each hummingbird is constructed from 53 individual pieces of abalone shell and mother-of-pearl, including 18 pieces within the wings alone. The botanical motif comprises 84 individual pieces.
Developing the compositions took more than nine months, as Rolls-Royce designers and craftspeople worked to overcome the technical challenges presented by the delicate material.
Abalone shell is unusually fine and brittle, requiring the Bespoke Collective’s designers, engineers and craftspeople to develop a suitable method for cutting, finishing and setting each individual fragment into the veneer.
Six iterations were required before the appropriate technique was established.
The final process begins by reducing the thickness of the pearl and abalone shell before each fragment is carefully set into place and lacquered.
Every piece is laser-cut 0.06mm larger than its final size to accommodate the laser’s burn margin. Each fragment is then filed by hand to achieve its precise final shape.
The edges of each piece are worked individually until they meet their neighbours without visible seams. This level of precision is particularly important for elements such as the hummingbird’s wings, where the craftspeople rely on hand-finishing to achieve the required fit.
Once the pieces have been cut and fitted, each Picnic Table and the Rear Waterfall panel requires a further eight hours to complete.
Across the three panels, the process represents approximately 45 hours of finishing work.
The abalone marquetry is complemented by an interior palette designed to emphasise the natural materials and colours of the composition.
Ash Burr veneer provides the background for all three marquetry panels, while Silver Birch features within the Picnic Table motifs.
The Silver Birch is cut entirely from a single log selected and examined in detail to ensure that its grain pattern complemented the overall design.
The seating is finished in Creme Light leather with Moccasin and Tan detailing, while Seashell carpets and a Starlight Headliner complete the interior suite.
The natural-inspired design continues across the exterior of Phantom Hummingbird.
The lower body is finished in Wildberry, contrasted with a White Sands upper body. A hand-applied White Sands Coachline traces the division between the two colours.
A hummingbird appears along the length of the Coachline, creating a visual connection between the exterior and the bespoke interior marquetry.
Through Phantom Hummingbird, Rolls-Royce has combined rare natural materials, painstaking handcraftsmanship and Bespoke automotive design to create a private commission centred on the changing colours and delicate beauty of the hummingbird.

title: Penang International Travel Exchange 2026 to Bring Global Buyers to Malaysia
bodyText:
The Penang International Travel Exchange (PITE) 2026 is set to return from 27 to 29 October 2026, bringing together international travel buyers and Malaysia’s tourism industry for three days of business networking, B2B engagements and destination experiences in Penang.
Now in its ninth edition, PITE 2026 will be held at the Penang Waterfront Convention Centre (PWCC). The programme will combine 1.5 days of structured business-to-business appointments with another 1.5 days of familiarisation activities and networking opportunities across the state.
The event is designed to strengthen connections between Malaysian tourism suppliers and international travel trade decision-makers while creating opportunities for new partnerships and business leads.
PITE 2026 is expected to welcome approximately 100 buyers from a broad range of travel trade segments, including corporate, incentive and association buyers.
The international buyer delegation will include representatives from China, India, Indonesia, Thailand, Vietnam, Singapore, Bangladesh, Australia, Romania and South Korea, alongside participants from other international markets.
The diverse representation reflects PITE’s objective of connecting Malaysian tourism businesses with decision-makers seeking new destinations, products and experiences for their respective clients and markets.
“PITE has evolved into an important platform for the tourism industry to connect, exchange ideas and create new business opportunities across borders. This year, we are particularly pleased to welcome a diverse group of buyers from both established and emerging markets, alongside Malaysian tourism industry players who are ready to showcase the breadth of products and experiences available across the country,” said YB Wong Hon Wai, Penang State Executive Councillor for Tourism and Creative Economy.
The B2B component of PITE 2026 will provide buyers and exhibitors with dedicated opportunities to explore potential partnerships, develop new business leads and strengthen existing relationships.
Through pre-arranged business appointments, participants will be able to engage directly with tourism businesses and explore products suited to different international markets.
Approximately 50 exhibitors from across Malaysia are expected to take part, representing a broad spectrum of the tourism ecosystem.
These include hoteliers, destination management companies (DMCs), professional conference organisers (PCOs), attractions and other tourism-related businesses.
The range of participating businesses will give international buyers an opportunity to discover Malaysia’s tourism products as well as its business events and related offerings.
Beyond the B2B sessions, PITE 2026 will take participants beyond the convention floor through a series of familiarisation trips across Penang.
The programme will give international buyers first-hand exposure to the state’s tourism products, hospitality offerings, cultural heritage and culinary experiences, while allowing them to experience Penang as a destination.
These familiarisation activities are intended to give buyers a deeper understanding of the products and experiences they can subsequently recommend and package for their respective markets.
By experiencing the destination directly, buyers can gain practical insight into Penang’s tourism offerings and identify opportunities that could appeal to travellers from their home markets.
PITE 2026 will also welcome approximately 10 international media representatives, who will have the opportunity to explore Penang and discover its latest tourism offerings.
Their participation is expected to support wider international destination awareness and provide additional exposure for Penang’s tourism industry.
The media programme complements PITE’s B2B focus by extending the event’s reach beyond travel trade participants and introducing Penang’s tourism experiences to international audiences.
With its combination of business-to-business engagement, destination familiarisation and networking, PITE 2026 aims to create commercial opportunities that can extend beyond the three-day event.
As international travel continues to evolve, the travel exchange provides Malaysian tourism stakeholders with an opportunity to better understand changing market needs, strengthen international relationships and position their products to a wider network of global buyers.
For Penang, the event also provides a platform to showcase the state’s tourism, hospitality, cultural and culinary offerings while strengthening its connections with the international travel trade.

title: ASB Calls for Stronger Workforce Transformation Focus in Budget 2027
bodyText:
As Malaysia prepares for the tabling of Budget 2027, the Asia School of Business (ASB) is calling for a stronger focus on workforce transformation to help Malaysian workers adapt as artificial intelligence (AI), automation and emerging technologies reshape jobs across the economy.
ASB said Malaysia’s competitiveness will depend not only on attracting investment and adopting new technologies, but also on ensuring that its workforce is equipped to adapt to changing roles and opportunities.
“Technology will change the way we work, but the question is whether our workforce is ready to change with it,” said Melati Nungsari, Deputy CEO and Deputy Dean of Research and Academics, Associate Professor of Economics, and Faculty Director of the ASEAN Research Center (ARC) at the Asia School of Business. “Malaysia has invested heavily in infrastructure and digitalisation. We now need to make a similar investment in our people, helping workers acquire new skills, move into new roles and work alongside new technologies,” she said.
Against this backdrop, ASB has identified four areas it believes should receive greater attention in Budget 2027, ranging from employer incentives and workforce development funding to job redesign and stronger industry-education partnerships.
ASB is urging the government to encourage employers to invest in structured workforce development through stronger, outcome-based incentives.
Rather than linking tax incentives primarily to the number of training hours completed, ASB recommends tying support to measurable outcomes such as improved productivity, career progression and wage growth.
The approach would place greater emphasis on whether training and reskilling programmes actually help employees move into higher-value roles and contribute more effectively to their organisations.
With AI and automation changing the skills required across industries, ASB said workforce development should focus not simply on increasing participation in training, but on helping workers acquire capabilities that translate into career and productivity gains.
ASB is also calling for greater flexibility in the use of the HRD Corp levy to support a wider range of workforce development needs.
The school recommends that existing funding mechanisms provide greater support for mid-career professionals, executive education and emerging areas such as AI, digital transformation and leadership.
This would allow organisations and employees to respond more quickly to changing skills requirements, particularly as businesses integrate new technologies into their operations.
The recommendation reflects the broader shift in workforce development, where employees may need to continuously update their capabilities rather than rely solely on skills acquired earlier in their careers.
As companies adopt AI and automation, ASB is advocating for government support that encourages businesses to redesign jobs and manage workforce transitions, rather than focusing solely on technology-driven replacement.
ASB recommends incentives that encourage companies to develop workforce transition plans covering redeployment, retraining and the creation of new, higher-value roles.
The aim is to help employees move alongside technological change and allow businesses to make better use of human capabilities as routine tasks become increasingly automated.
This approach would also support the creation of roles that complement new technologies, allowing workers to develop skills that remain relevant as the nature of work evolves.
ASB’s fourth recommendation is to strengthen partnerships between industry and education providers.
The school said government, businesses and universities should work more closely to identify emerging skills requirements and develop shorter, practical programmes that can respond more quickly to changing industry needs.
Closer collaboration could help education providers better understand the capabilities employers require while giving businesses greater access to talent equipped for emerging roles.
ASB said demand for leadership, digital fluency and applied AI capabilities has grown through its executive education programmes as organisations navigate workforce transformation.
“Our recommendations are informed by ASB’s work with corporate and government partners through its executive education programmes, where demand for leadership, digital fluency and applied AI capabilities has grown as organisations navigate workforce transformation,” said Melati.
Ultimately, ASB said the objective should not simply be to train more people, but to ensure Malaysians can continue creating value as the nature of work changes.
By combining workforce upskilling with job redesign, flexible funding and stronger collaboration between industry and education providers, Malaysia can better prepare its workforce for technological change.
For ASB, strengthening human capital alongside digitalisation and investment will be important to positioning Malaysia for sustainable, high-value economic growth under Budget 2027.

title: Mercedes-Benz Malaysia Previews All-New CLA 200 AMG Line with Electrified Powertrain
bodyText:
Mercedes-Benz Malaysia has previewed the locally assembled all-new Mercedes-Benz CLA 200 AMG Line in Singapore, introducing an internal combustion engine counterpart to the recently launched fully electric CLA.
The new model gives Malaysian customers greater choice between powertrains while bringing together the distinctive CLA design with electrified performance, intelligent technology and enhanced comfort.
As a locally assembled model, the CLA 200 AMG Line is positioned within Mercedes-Benz’s latest compact vehicle portfolio and is designed to combine everyday usability with improved efficiency.
“The all-new Mercedes-Benz CLA 200 AMG Line reflects our commitment to offering customers in Malaysia the freedom to choose the powertrain that best suits their needs. As a locally assembled model, it combines the unmistakable character of the CLA with outstanding efficiency, intelligent technology, and elevated comfort, complementing the all-new electric CLA within our most advanced compact vehicle portfolio yet,” said Martin Schulz, CEO & President, Mercedes-Benz Cars Malaysia and Head of Region, Mercedes-Benz Cars Southeast Asia.
Kevin Barbian, Chief Operating Officer (COO), Mercedes-Benz Cars Malaysia, said the model balances its expressive design with efficient everyday driving.
“The all-new Mercedes-Benz CLA 200 AMG Line offers customers an ideal balance of expressive design and effortless everyday driving. Its distinctive illuminated radiator grille creates an unmistakable presence, while the ability to drive on electric power at urban speeds, coast efficiently, and recuperate energy across all eight gears delivers a smooth and highly efficient driving experience,” he said.
The CLA 200 AMG Line features a new electrified eight-speed dual-clutch transmission with an integrated electric motor. This allows the vehicle to drive on electric power under certain urban driving conditions, coast with the drivetrain decoupled and recover energy through regenerative braking.
With fuel consumption of around five litres per 100 kilometres and below, Mercedes-Benz positions the CLA 200 AMG Line as its most efficient vehicle with an internal combustion engine in this segment.
The vehicle is powered by a 1.5-litre engine producing 163hp, with a system output of 184hp and system torque of 330Nm. It accelerates from 0 to 100km/h in 8.0 seconds and has a top speed of 232km/h.
The electrified powertrain also allows electric driving at urban speeds when less than 22kW of power is required, typically during gentle town driving.
The CLA can also engage in what Mercedes-Benz describes as “electric sailing”, allowing it to coast efficiently with the drivetrain decoupled at speeds of up to around 100km/h.
Another feature is the ability to recuperate energy in all eight gears, recovering up to 25kW of energy. The electric motor can also start the combustion engine without the need for a conventional pinion starter, helping make engine starts and transitions between the two motors almost imperceptible.
At the heart of the electrified system is the new 8G-eDCT eight-speed dual-clutch transmission, which integrates the electric motor and its components directly into the transmission.
This compact arrangement helps keep the powertrain efficient while conserving space within the vehicle.
The electric motor is powered by a new 48-volt lithium-ion battery with an energy content of up to 1.3kWh. The battery has been designed to be compact and lightweight, supporting the vehicle’s electrified driving capabilities without requiring a dedicated high-voltage battery system.
Visually, the all-new CLA 200 AMG Line closely follows the design of its fully electric counterpart.
The locally assembled model features an AMG Line exterior, 19-inch AMG 5-twin-spoke light-alloy wheels, MULTIBEAM LED headlights, surround lighting with animated Mercedes-Benz pattern projections and a large panoramic roof.
Five exterior paint finishes are available: Cosmic Black, Polar White, High-Tech Silver, Sheer Blue and Aqua Mint.
One of the key visual differences between the combustion-engine CLA and its electric sibling is the front grille.
The CLA 200 features a classic radiator grille with a central Mercedes-Benz star and chrome Mercedes-Benz pattern. It is framed by an LED light guide, with illuminated edges when the headlights are switched on.
Inside, the CLA 200 AMG Line shares much of the technology found in the fully electric CLA.
Mercedes-Benz Operating System (MB.OS) and the fourth-generation MBUX infotainment system underpin the vehicle’s digital experience, with artificial intelligence from Microsoft and Google integrated into MBUX.
The MBUX Virtual Assistant uses a multi-agent approach, selecting the most suitable AI source for different tasks. This allows drivers to interact with the system conversationally and receive answers and follow-up information without repeatedly providing the same context.
The vehicle’s software can also receive over-the-air updates, including updates to driving assistance systems. Mercedes-Benz said this allows the CLA to receive new functions and improvements throughout its ownership period.
The all-new CLA also introduces a navigation experience based on Google Maps, developed through a partnership between Google and Mercedes-Benz.
The system integrates Google Cloud’s Automotive AI Agent with Google Maps, while MBUX Navigation combines route guidance with a real-time 3D representation of the vehicle’s surroundings.
The integration is designed to provide drivers with greater situational awareness by displaying what the vehicle detects and how its assistance systems are supporting the driver.
Safety and driver assistance features include Distance Assist DISTRONIC, while additional comfort and assistance functions are bundled under MB.DRIVE.
The CLA also comes with MB.DRIVE PARKING ASSIST 360, providing additional support when manoeuvring and parking.
The cabin combines AMG Line styling with a fully digital interior.
These systems complement the model’s wider suite of safety and assistance technologies, bringing the CLA in line with Mercedes-Benz’s latest approach to connected and assisted driving.
The all-new CLA 200 AMG Line features an AMG Line Sports Seat Package, ARTICO leather and MICROCUT microfibre upholstery, light carbon-grain aluminium trim elements and a multifunction sports steering wheel in Nappa leather.
Dominating the dashboard is the floating MBUX Superscreen, which stretches across the width of the interior behind a large glass surface.
It incorporates a 10.25-inch driver display, a 14-inch central display and a 14-inch front passenger display.
The front passenger display provides access to more than 40 apps, video streaming and Disney+, while all three displays are powered by high-performance chips and real-time graphics from the Unity Game Engine.
For additional cabin comfort, THERMOTRONIC automatic climate control allows the driver and front passenger to set their preferred temperatures independently.
The locally assembled Mercedes-Benz CLA 200 AMG Line is now available for pre-booking at an estimated price starting from RM275,000 for Peninsular Malaysia.
The first 100 customers who pre-book the model will each receive passes to the upcoming exclusive Mercedes-AMG F1 Party, subject to terms and conditions.
Mercedes-Benz is also offering its Agility+ ownership plan for the new CLA 200 AMG Line, with estimated monthly repayments starting from RM2,888.
The plan includes a fifth-year extended limited warranty, Star Gold, and four Compact Service Packages, alongside flexible end-of-term options and the MobilityPlus programme.
The MobilityPlus programme provides a guaranteed temporary Mercedes-Benz replacement car when a vehicle is undergoing service, maintenance or warrantable repairs for 48 hours or more, subject to terms and conditions.
For more information, customers can visit the Mercedes-Benz Malaysia website or speak to a Finance and Insurance Executive at their nearest Mercedes-Benz Autohaus.

title: Mercedes-Benz Malaysia Previews All-New Electric GLC with Up to 616km Range
bodyText:
Mercedes-Benz Malaysia has presented an early preview of the all-new electric Mercedes-Benz GLC in Singapore, bringing the brand’s globally best-selling model into the electric era with a purpose-developed electric architecture.
The new Mercedes-Benz GLC 300 4MATIC electric combines a 310kW (421hp) electric drive system with 800Nm of torque and an electric range of up to 616 kilometres according to WLTP.
Its 800-volt electrical architecture supports DC fast charging of up to 320kW, allowing the vehicle to add up to 255km of WLTP range in 10 minutes under suitable charging conditions.
In Malaysia, the all-new electric GLC will be offered in two variants: the GLC 300 4MATIC electric AVANTGARDE, with an estimated price from RM389,000, and the GLC 300 4MATIC electric AMG Line Plus, estimated from RM399,000.
The all-new electric GLC retains the proportions of the Mercedes-Benz midsize SUV while introducing a new design language developed for the electric era.
Its front is defined by an illuminated grille featuring a wide chrome frame, smoked-glass-look mesh structure and integrated contour lighting. The grille incorporates 942 individually backlit polycarbonate dots, creating an animated pixel graphic, while the central Mercedes-Benz star and surrounding contour are also illuminated.
The DIGITAL LIGHT headlights complement the grille, with the Mercedes-Benz star and visor-style daytime running lights, marker lights and indicators reinforcing the vehicle’s identity.
At the rear, two-part tail lights feature a star motif that animates when the vehicle is unlocked or charging. The AMG Line Plus adds an AMG spoiler lip for a sportier appearance.
Aerodynamic detailing also contributes to an aerodynamic drag coefficient of Cd 0.26, supporting the vehicle’s efficiency.
The AVANTGARDE rides on 20-inch multi-spoke light-alloy wheels, while the AMG Line Plus features 21-inch AMG multi-spoke light-alloy wheels.
The GLC 300 4MATIC electric is available in Obsidian Black, MANUFAKTUR Opalite White Bright, High-Tech Silver, Lavender Silver and Sodalite Blue. The AMG Line Plus adds MANUFAKTUR Alpine Grey Solid and MANUFAKTUR Patagonia Red Metallic.
Inside, the electric GLC combines Mercedes-Benz’s focus on luxury with an increasingly digital driving experience.
At the centre is the new seamless MBUX HYPERSCREEN, measuring 99.3 centimetres (39.1 inches) across the width of the cockpit. It uses high-resolution displays and matrix backlighting with more than 1,000 individual LEDs.
The fourth generation of Mercedes-Benz User Experience (MBUX) is powered by MB.OS, the company’s operating system designed to allow the vehicle’s functions and digital services to evolve through updates.
The enhanced MBUX Zero Layer places frequently used information, suggestions and applications within easy reach, while users can organise applications into personalised folders in a smartphone-style interface.
The system also incorporates real-time graphics powered by the Unity Game Engine and a display algorithm designed to improve readability in sunlight.
Artificial intelligence plays a larger role in the fourth-generation MBUX system, which integrates AI from Microsoft and Google.
The MBUX Virtual Assistant uses a “Multi Agent Approach” to handle different types of requests within the same conversation. Depending on the context, it can draw on different sources for navigation, general knowledge or vehicle-related questions.
The system supports more natural, multi-turn conversations and can retain context throughout an interaction.
For general knowledge, ChatGPT and Microsoft Bing Search operate as agents, while Google Cloud’s Automotive AI Agent provides navigation-related assistance using information from the Google Maps platform.
A third agent acts as a vehicle expert, providing information about the driver’s own car.
The virtual assistant can be activated using the familiar “Hey Mercedes” command and appears as an animated Mercedes-Benz star on the Zero Layer. Additional avatar designs include a human-like representation and the expressive “LittleBenz” character.
The electric GLC also offers greater interior space, supported by a 2,972mm wheelbase, which is eight centimetres longer than that of the combustion-engine GLC.
Front passengers gain an additional 13mm of legroom, while rear passengers gain 47mm. Headroom increases by 46mm at the front and 17mm at the rear.
Luggage capacity stands at 570 litres behind the rear seats and increases to 1,740 litres with the rear backrests folded. A further 128 litres of storage is available in the front luggage compartment, or frunk.
The rear seat backrest can be electrically folded in a 40:20:40 split, while the Boot Comfort Package allows the loading floor to be lowered by 80mm for taller objects.
The AVANTGARDE features comfort seats available in black or beech brown/black leather upholstery, while the AMG Line Plus comes with the AMG Line Sports Seat Package in black leather with contrasting red topstitching.
Both seat types use a one-piece manufacturing process and feature double stitching.
Heat- and noise-insulating acoustic glass contributes to a quieter cabin, while ambient lighting extends across the dashboard, doors and SKY CONTROL panoramic roof.
The switchable panoramic roof can transition between transparent and opaque states and is divided into nine individually adjustable segments.
At night, 162 integrated illuminated stars can create a starry-sky effect, with 64 available colours or synchronisation with the selected ambient lighting theme.
The Mercedes-Benz GLC 300 4MATIC electric produces 310kW (421hp) and 800Nm of torque, accelerating from 0 to 100km/h in 4.7 seconds before reaching a top speed of 210km/h.
Its 85kWh usable battery provides a WLTP range of between 523km and 616km, depending on specification and conditions.
The electric drivetrain uses a permanently excited synchronous motor at the rear, developed in-house by Mercedes-Benz, with a two-speed gearbox designed to combine acceleration and efficiency.
The first gear supports acceleration, urban driving and towing, while the second gear is optimised for higher speeds and motorway efficiency.
The all-wheel-drive system can engage or disengage the front electric drive unit when required, supporting energy efficiency while maintaining traction.
One of the key features of the new electric GLC is its 800-volt electrical architecture.
DC fast charging is supported at up to 320kW, with the battery capable of charging from 10% to 80% in approximately 22 minutes under suitable conditions. Mercedes-Benz states that up to 215–255km of WLTP range can be added within 10 minutes, depending on conditions.
The vehicle also supports AC charging at up to 22kW, with a full 0–100% charge taking approximately four hours using a suitable 22kW AC charger.
The 85kWh lithium-ion battery uses an anode combining silicon oxide with graphite, while the battery architecture has been designed for modularity, serviceability and manufacturing flexibility.
The electric GLC also incorporates Mercedes-Benz Navigation with Electric Intelligence, which automatically plans charging stops based on factors including route conditions, topography, temperature, traffic, driving style and available charging infrastructure.
The system can also take charging capacity, payment options and weather information into account when calculating energy requirements.
Charging stops can be adjusted dynamically, while the system preconditions the high-voltage battery to help achieve optimal DC charging performance when the vehicle reaches a selected charging station.
Through MB.CHARGE Public, drivers can access public charging networks using a single charging contract. Charging costs can be viewed through the MBUX display or Mercedes-Benz app, including the cost per kilowatt-hour or minute and estimated total charging cost.
Beyond ECO, COMFORT, SPORT and INDIVIDUAL driving modes, the electric GLC introduces a TERRAIN mode for dirt and gravel roads.
When activated, the front axle of the 4MATIC system automatically engages while the drivetrain, steering and braking characteristics are adjusted.
When equipped with DIGITAL LIGHT, the off-road lighting function can provide wider illumination to help drivers identify obstacles.
The “transparent bonnet” function, used with MB.DRIVE PARKING ASSIST 360, provides a virtual view of the area beneath the front of the vehicle. Camera images from the front and exterior mirror cameras are combined on the central display, with a trajectory overlay helping drivers select a suitable path.
The all-new electric GLC comes with an extensive suite of safety and driver assistance technologies.
Its hardware includes up to 10 cameras, five radar sensors and 12 ultrasonic sensors, supported by a high-performance computer designed to accommodate future functions and over-the-air updates.
Mercedes-Benz also offers the MB.DRIVE suite of assistance features.
MB.DRIVE ASSIST combines Distance Assist DISTRONIC with Steering Assist to provide a SAE Level 2 driving assistance system. Steering Assist helps keep the vehicle centred in its lane, while Lane Change Assist can facilitate lane changes when the indicator stalk is operated.
MB.DRIVE PARKING ASSIST 360 adds enhanced surround-view displays using a 360-degree camera.
The vehicle also features PRE-SAFE occupant protection technology, up to 11 airbags and an MBUX dashcam.
The MBUX system supports more than 40 apps across categories including audio, video, productivity and entertainment, with the portfolio set to expand over time.
The system supports video streaming while the vehicle is stationary, while the front passenger can continue to use selected video functions while driving.
The in-car app store also provides access to video conferencing applications, including the updated “Meetings for Teams” app.
Disney+ is available through the MBUX infotainment system in more than 40 countries, subject to the relevant Digital Extra and an active subscription.
The electric GLC also supports Dolby Atmos through Apple CarPlay, while Mercedes-Benz’s Sound Experience provides several personalised acoustic environments.
Mercedes-Benz said the all-new electric GLC achieves a two-thirds reduction in carbon footprint across its lifecycle compared with the current combustion-powered GLC.
More than two-thirds of the vehicle’s aluminium requirements are sourced as carbon-reduced aluminium, including components such as the body, steering knuckles, wheels and battery housing.
The new battery generation also achieves an approximately 30% reduction in carbon footprint per cell compared with conventional production, supported by carbon reduction measures across cell manufacturing and the use of renewable energy.
The company is also increasing the use of secondary and renewable materials. The seat foam, for example, contains around 30% recycled content using the mass-balance approach.
The all-new electric GLC will be produced at the Mercedes-Benz Bremen plant alongside vehicles with conventional drivetrains.
The plant uses 100% green electricity and operates net carbon-neutrally for the production of the model.
Electric drive units are supplied from Sebes in Romania, electric axles from Hamburg and batteries from Kamenz in Germany.
Mercedes-Benz said the electric GLC forms part of a flexible global production network, with models based on the new electric architecture also set to be produced in Kecskemét, Hungary, and Beijing, China.
The all-new Mercedes-Benz GLC 300 4MATIC electric AVANTGARDE and GLC 300 4MATIC electric AMG Line Plus are available for pre-booking in Malaysia at estimated prices starting from RM389,000 and RM399,000, respectively.
The first 100 customers who pre-book the all-new electric GLC will receive passes to the upcoming exclusive Mercedes-AMG F1 Party, subject to terms and conditions.
Mercedes-Benz Malaysia is also offering the Agility+ financing plan from an estimated RM4,288 per month for the AVANTGARDE and RM4,388 per month for the AMG Line Plus.
The plan includes a fifth-year extended limited warranty, Star Gold and four Compact Service Packages, with additional terms and conditions applying.
The all-new electric GLC marks Mercedes-Benz Malaysia’s latest move to expand its electric vehicle offering, combining the familiar midsize SUV format with longer-range electric driving, rapid charging and a more connected digital experience.

title: Creative Sprint 2026 Helps Malaysian Social Enterprises Build for Sustainable Growth
bodyText:
Twenty-one social enterprises from Central and Northern Malaysia have completed Creative Sprint 2026, a venture development programme designed to help purpose-driven businesses strengthen their foundations for sustainable growth and greater social impact.
Now in its third year, Satu Creative’s flagship programme brought together founders working across three themes: Income Pathways, Heritage Conservation and Circular Solutions.
The programme encouraged participating founders to look beyond their social purpose and examine the fundamentals needed to build businesses that can last, including understanding customers, strengthening revenue models, measuring impact, developing partnerships and identifying suitable capital for growth.
Across its Kuala Lumpur and Penang editions, participants put these principles into practice through intensive bootcamps, gaining direct access to entrepreneurs, investors, industry practitioners and ecosystem leaders.
For social enterprises, creating positive social or environmental impact is closely linked to building a financially sustainable business model.
“Across both cohorts, we saw founders with a strong sense of purpose and a willingness to challenge their assumptions. Creative Sprint gives them the space to test ideas, learn from those who have been there, build the right connections and get clearer on what comes next. What matters now is how they turn those insights into action and impact,” said Ahmad Azuar Zainuddin, Chief Executive Officer of Satu Creative.
Throughout the programme, participating founders were able to engage with experienced entrepreneurs, investors and ecosystem leaders, gaining perspectives on areas ranging from business development and investment readiness to partnerships and market opportunities.
Among those involved were Tuan Haji Hazani Hassan of Malaysian Technology Development Corporation (MTDC), Sam Shafie of pitchIN, Lilyana Latiff of BETA Foundation, Joe Sidek of Penang Arts Council, Aaron Sarma of ScaleUp Malaysia, Johnathan Lee of Cradle Fund, Andy Othman of Plug and Play Malaysia, Khooi Chu Boon of Digital Penang, Howie Chang of Forward College, Jian Tong Chia of White Room and Wan Dazriq Wan Zulkiflee of SEEd.Lab.
Bank Simpanan Nasional (BSN) also led a dedicated session for participating founders.
The programme culminated in Pitch Days in Kuala Lumpur and Penang, where participants presented their ventures to mentors, investors and ecosystem leaders.
With support from Yayasan Hasanah, Bank Simpanan Nasional, Digital Penang, Malaysian Business Angels Network (MBAN) and Artem Ventures, Creative Sprint provided founders with feedback, networks and potential pathways to funding, partnerships and market opportunities.
The programme is designed not only to help social enterprises refine their ideas, but also to strengthen their ability to translate those ideas into viable ventures capable of sustaining their social impact over the longer term.
For the participating social enterprises, completing Creative Sprint is only one stage of their wider growth journey.
Eligible ventures will have the opportunity to receive grants of up to RM100,000 to support their next stage of development, alongside the networks and opportunities established through the programme.
Yayasan Hasanah said access to funding, knowledge and networks can help social enterprises strengthen their businesses while expanding their impact.
“Social enterprises have an important role to play in addressing the needs of communities, but creating lasting impact also requires strong and sustainable businesses,” said Puan Siti Kamariah Ahmad Subki, Managing Director and Trustee, Yayasan Hasanah. “Through the Hasanah Social Enterprise Fund and our collaboration with Satu Creative, we are supporting founders with access to funding, knowledge and networks that can help them strengthen their ventures and grow their impact,” she said.
She added that Yayasan Hasanah was encouraged by this year’s participants and looked forward to seeing how their ventures develop.
With the programme completed, the focus now shifts to implementation as participating founders apply what they have learned to their ventures.
For Satu Creative, the objective is to help social enterprises move from purpose-driven ideas towards stronger business models, deeper partnerships and sustainable growth.
The next stage will see eligible ventures pursue funding and other opportunities while continuing to build the capabilities needed to expand their reach and deepen their impact.
Creative Sprint 2026 ultimately highlights the connection between social impact and business sustainability, demonstrating how stronger commercial foundations can help purpose-driven enterprises continue serving their communities over the long term.

title: PIKOM Digital Excellence Awards 2026 Honour Record 102 Technology Winners
bodyText:
A record 102 technology players were recognised at the PIKOM Digital Excellence Awards (PDEA) 2026, more than double the 52 winners recorded last year, reflecting the growing breadth of Malaysia’s digital ecosystem.
A highlight of the awards was the presentation of the PIKOM Tech Luminary Award to Datuk (Dr) Yasmin Mahmood for her leadership, influence and contribution to Malaysia’s technology industry.
Yasmin, currently Executive Chairman of Jasa Kita Berhad, previously served as Chief Executive Officer of the Malaysia Digital Economy Corporation (MDEC), where she played a key role in advancing Malaysia’s digital economy and strengthening the country’s position on the global technology stage.
The awards gala brought together more than 1,100 industry leaders, government representatives and technology professionals, making it the largest dinner in the history of PIKOM, which is marking its 40th anniversary this year.
PIKOM Chairman Adjunct Professor (Practice) Alex Liew said the record number of participants demonstrated the strength and diversity of Malaysia’s technology ecosystem.
He stressed that the increase in award recipients did not make the PDEA easier to win, with every submission required to meet stringent qualification requirements before undergoing independent assessment against defined criteria.
PDEA has grown steadily since its inaugural edition in 2024, when 34 winners were recognised. The number increased to 52 winners in 2025 before reaching 102 this year.
New categories were also introduced in 2026 to recognise emerging innovations that are reshaping industries and creating new opportunities.
Liew said the winners demonstrated Malaysia’s ability to develop technology solutions with regional and global relevance.
“We hope the recognition will strengthen confidence in their organisations, motivate their teams and help showcase Malaysian capabilities to the region and the world,” he said.
PDEA winners may also have opportunities to represent Malaysia at regional and international awards organised by the Asian-Oceanian Computing Industry Organization, the Asia Pacific ICT Alliance and the World Innovation, Technology and Services Alliance.
The awards also highlighted the importance of developing homegrown technology as Malaysia works towards becoming an AI Nation by 2030.
Digital Minister Gobind Singh Deo said Malaysia must move beyond simply adopting technologies developed elsewhere. His speech was delivered on his behalf by Malaysia Digital Economy Corporation (MDEC) Chairman Ganesh Kumar Bangah.
“True digital sovereignty means moving from being passive consumers and manufacturing hubs to becoming creators, leaders, and owners of the very tools, architectures, and platforms driving the global economy,” Gobind said.
He called on the digital industry to work more closely with the government on practical regulatory environments, industry-led talent development and the effective implementation of national digital strategies.
“Government policies set the trajectory, but the private sector dictates the velocity. PIKOM is uniquely positioned to help the government accelerate its digital ambitions,” he said.
Gobind also urged Malaysian technology companies to strengthen the country’s role as a technology bridge for Southeast Asia.
This includes developing interoperable platforms and localised artificial intelligence models that reflect the region’s languages, markets and security priorities.
He also highlighted the need to make AI and advanced digital solutions more accessible to micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs).
For smaller businesses, digital adoption is increasingly becoming a matter of survival rather than an optional investment, reinforcing the need for technology solutions that can be adopted across different segments of the economy.
Industry players were also encouraged to submit their views and proposals for Budget 2027 through the Ministry of Finance’s official portal.
The PDEA gala dinner also commemorated PIKOM’s 40th anniversary under the theme “Celebration, Recognition and Inclusivity”.
As part of the anniversary celebrations, PIKOM paid tribute to its 21 past chairmen and recognised 41 member companies that have supported the association for between 25 and 40 years.
“As PIKOM enters its fifth decade, we will remain a bridge between government and industry, established leaders and emerging talent, and Malaysia and the global digital economy,” Liew said.
The association also expressed its appreciation to its 2026 corporate partners Maxis, U Mobile and China Mobile International, as well as media partner Media Prima, for supporting the awards and its wider industry initiatives.
The record turnout and expanded awards programme mark another milestone for PIKOM as it enters its fifth decade, while highlighting the growing range of Malaysian companies contributing to the country’s digital economy and technology landscape.

title: ‘Remarkable Shandong’ Agricultural Trade Expo Returns to Malaysia with Nearly 100 Companies
bodyText:
The “Remarkable Shandong” Agricultural Trade (Malaysia) Expo 2026 officially opened at the Kuala Lumpur Convention Centre (KLCC), bringing nearly 100 companies from six cities across Shandong and more than 1,100 products to Malaysia for three days of trade and industry engagement.
Returning for its second edition, the Expo places greater emphasis this year on halal standards, market access and cross-border supply chain cooperation, connecting Shandong producers with Malaysian buyers, distributors and industry partners while opening pathways to the wider ASEAN market.
The opening ceremony brought together representatives from Shandong, Malaysian government agencies, business chambers, buyers, exhibitors and the media. Among the guests were Dato’ Dr Fathul Bari bin Mat Jahya, Chairman of UiTM Holdings Sdn Bhd; YB Tan Kok Wai, Former Special Envoy of the Prime Minister of Malaysia to China and Former Chairman of the Malaysia-China Business Council; Dato’ See Meng Geok, Vice President of the Malaysia-China Chamber of Commerce (MCCC); and Duan Youchen, Deputy Secretary of the Party Committee and Vice Chairman of Shandong Agricultural Group Co., Ltd.
The guests jointly launched the Expo, marking the official opening of its second Malaysian edition.
Shandong is one of China’s major agricultural provinces, with an extensive ecosystem spanning farming and livestock, food processing, cold-chain logistics and agricultural equipment.
In 2025, the province’s total output value across agriculture, forestry, animal husbandry and fisheries exceeded RMB1.3 trillion, while agricultural exports reached RMB166.83 billion, representing a 1.2% year-on-year increase. Shandong has also ranked first in China for agricultural exports for 26 consecutive years, accounting for 22.4% of the country’s total agricultural exports.
The inaugural Expo in 2025 brought together 69 companies from 16 cities across Shandong, showcasing more than 800 products and attracting nearly 230 government, business and trade association representatives from Malaysia and China.
The event connected participating companies with buyers from several ASEAN markets and generated more than RMB100 million in potential transactions, alongside strategic agreements, orders and longer-term supply arrangements.
Building on this momentum, the 2026 edition has expanded its scale and product offering through cross-border B2B business matching, new product launches, product showcases and halal industry engagement.
The Expo aims to bring more quality Shandong agricultural products into Malaysia and ASEAN while creating sustainable distribution and supply chain partnerships.
Malaysia’s established halal ecosystem provides an important platform for Shandong companies looking to enter the Malaysian market and reach Muslim consumers across ASEAN.
According to the Halal Development Corporation Berhad (HDC), Malaysia’s halal exports reached RM68.52 billion in 2025, representing a 10.9% year-on-year increase.
For companies entering the Malaysian halal market, however, compliance extends beyond product labelling. Businesses must understand ingredient sourcing, production processes, traceability, warehousing, logistics and certification requirements across the supply chain.
“Shandong is one of China’s major agricultural provinces. In 2025, the total output value of its agriculture, forestry, animal husbandry and fisheries exceeded RMB1.3 trillion, while its agricultural exports have ranked first in China for 26 consecutive years. Malaysia is not only an important economic and trade partner for Shandong in ASEAN, but also an important gateway to ASEAN and the global halal market,” said Duan Youchen, Deputy Secretary of the Party Committee and Vice Chairman of Shandong Agricultural Group Co., Ltd.
He said the Expo aims to establish platforms for two-way trade in quality agricultural products, cooperation across the agricultural value chain and international promotion of agricultural brands.
“By leveraging Malaysia’s established halal certification ecosystem, we also hope to support more quality Shandong agricultural products in reaching ASEAN and international markets, while taking agricultural cooperation into broader areas and to greater depth,” he added.
Dato’ Dr Fathul Bari bin Mat Jahya, Chairman of UiTM Holdings Sdn Bhd, said the Expo brings together nearly 100 companies from six cities across Shandong, showcasing more than 1,100 products and the province’s capabilities in agricultural production, food processing and supply chains.
“For businesses, having a quality product is only the first step towards entering a market. The right packaging and labelling, consistent quality and supply, and reliable local partners are equally important,” he said.
He also highlighted the five strategic cooperation agreements expected to be facilitated at the Expo, covering agricultural trade, agri-food products, beef, the halal industry, and trade and investment promotion.
“We hope this Expo will serve as a starting point to bring together industry, technology and knowledge, helping more Shandong companies find long-term partners in Malaysia and translating these connections into tangible outcomes,” he said.
YB Tan Kok Wai, Former Special Envoy of the Prime Minister of Malaysia to China and Former Chairman of the Malaysia-China Business Council, said closer agricultural cooperation between Malaysia and China carries both economic and strategic significance.
He highlighted China’s experience in modern agricultural technology, food processing, cold-chain logistics and agricultural machinery, while noting Shandong’s position as China’s leading agricultural export province.
“We welcome more quality Shandong products into Malaysia and hope Shandong companies will view Malaysia as an important partner and gateway to the ASEAN market,” he said.
The Expo also highlights the potential for cooperation to move beyond bilateral Malaysia-China trade.
Dato’ See Meng Geok, Vice President of the Malaysia-China Chamber of Commerce, said both sides could combine their respective strengths to pursue opportunities in wider international markets.
Shandong brings capabilities in agriculture, food processing, agricultural technology and supply chains, while Malaysia offers an established halal certification ecosystem and connectivity to ASEAN, the Middle East and global halal markets.
“We look forward to exploring a model that combines Shandong’s production capabilities with Malaysia’s halal certification and global market connectivity, positioning Malaysia as an important platform for quality Shandong products to reach international markets,” she said.
MCCC will continue to support business connections between the two sides and help develop opportunities across ASEAN, the Middle East and global markets.
According to the latest list published by the Department of Islamic Development Malaysia (JAKIM), 96 foreign halal certification bodies across 49 countries and regions are currently recognised. Six are located in China, including the Shandong Halal Certification Service (SHC) in Jinan.
The halal certification status of individual products exhibited at the Expo remains subject to valid documentation issued by the respective companies and relevant certification bodies.
The Expo showcases the breadth of Shandong’s agricultural industries and regional specialities, with products spanning fresh fruits and vegetables, grains and dry goods, prepared foods, meat and seafood, food ingredients and condiments, tea and beverages, and dairy products.
Five Malaysian organisations, including HDC, are also participating in the exhibition, strengthening local industry involvement and creating further opportunities for Shandong businesses to engage with Malaysian partners.
Following the opening ceremony, the “Remarkable Shandong” Premium Agri-Products Promotion in Malaysia Conference featured remarks by Bi Haixin, Level-II Bureau Level Official of the Shandong Provincial Department of Agriculture and Rural Affairs.
Presentations were also delivered by Su Kewei, Vice General Manager of Qilu Evening News · Qilu Yidian and Person in Charge of Shandong Qilu Nongchao Technology Co., Ltd.; and Liu Ting, Minister of the Market Department of Shandong Agricultural Group Agricultural Products Supply Chain Co., Ltd.
Representatives from Linyi City, Shen County, Yangxin County, Boxing County, Anqiu City and Linqu County also presented their respective agricultural strengths, signature products and potential areas for cooperation.
A key outcome of the Expo was the signing of five strategic cooperation agreements between Shandong companies and Malaysian and regional partners.
The agreements involved:
The five agreements cover agricultural trade, agri-food, beef and halal industries, as well as trade and investment promotion.
Together, they connect Shandong’s production and supply chain resources with commercial networks in Malaysia and the wider region, creating potential pathways for product procurement, market expansion, distribution development and longer-term supply chain partnerships.
The agreements underline the Expo’s broader objective of moving beyond product showcasing towards tangible business opportunities and deeper cooperation between Shandong and Malaysia across the agricultural and food industries.

title: Red Hat AI 3.5 Strengthens Enterprise AI with Safety, Governance and Observability
bodyText:
As businesses move from experimenting with artificial intelligence (AI) to deploying it at scale, Red Hat has introduced Red Hat AI 3.5, bringing new safety, observability and operational capabilities to its enterprise AI portfolio.
The latest release is designed to help IT and platform engineering teams manage AI with the same operational discipline applied to mission-critical infrastructure.
Red Hat said that while many organisations have successfully moved through AI pilots and early deployments, scaling these workloads across the business introduces new challenges around safety, resource management, governance and performance.
Red Hat AI 3.5 aims to address these challenges by providing a foundation for controlling, securing and observing AI workloads across hybrid cloud environments.
A major addition in Red Hat AI 3.5 is EvalHub, which enables organisations to evaluate AI models before they are deployed.
The capability is designed to support risk-focused safety benchmarking and the creation of regulatory compliance certifications, helping organisations assess potential risks before models, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems and AI agents are put into production.
Evaluated models in the Red Hat AI Catalog also feature built-in Garak benchmark scores, while more than 20 new validated models have been added to the catalogue.
These include models from Google, NVIDIA and Alibaba Cloud, among others.
The validated models now include integrated scores covering AI safety, personally identifiable information (PII) exposure and toxicity risks, giving enterprises greater visibility when assessing potential model risks.
A selection of validated models has also been tagged for tool-calling, providing additional guidance for organisations selecting models for agentic AI applications.
Red Hat AI 3.5 introduces new observability dashboards designed to give platform teams real-time insight into AI infrastructure and application performance.
The dashboards provide metrics covering inference health, GPU utilisation and AI model performance.
Non-administrator users can also access dashboards showing per-user token consumption, supporting greater transparency around AI usage and cost attribution.
For organisations operating AI as a shared service, these capabilities can help teams understand how resources are being consumed across users, models and workloads.
The release also adds MLflow visual agentic tracing, providing greater visibility into the behaviour and performance of AI agents.
As AI workloads place growing demands on GPU infrastructure, Red Hat AI 3.5 expands its multi-tenancy capabilities to help organisations manage shared computing resources.
Fair-share GPU scheduling allows organisations to manage resource allocation across tenants, while priority-aware serving provides admission control and priority-based request routing.
This allows real-time inference workloads to receive priority while background workloads can make use of available capacity.
For organisations requiring stronger isolation between tenants, Red Hat AI now officially supports hosted control planes on Red Hat OpenShift Virtualization.
Each tenant can have a dedicated cluster control plane while the underlying hardware is consolidated. AI workloads running in OpenShift Virtualization virtual machines can also benefit from VM-level isolation across shared, GPU-enabled infrastructure.
Red Hat said these capabilities allow infrastructure providers to operate and upgrade the underlying environment from a single point of control.
Red Hat AI 3.5 also expands capabilities for organisations developing and deploying agentic AI.
Its AutoRAG technology connects enterprise data repositories with agentic applications while adding support for multilingual documents, conversational testing and contextual retrieval.
A visual pipeline allows teams to test and assess RAG configurations before deployment, while pre-configured agent templates provide starting points for common enterprise applications.
These include code review, document processing and research workflows.
The AI Hub also introduces agent development kits and starter kits that integrate frameworks, tools and deployment configurations, allowing agents to operate within sandboxed environments while retaining operational controls and security policies from development through production.
Red Hat AI 3.5 introduces Inference-Time Scaling (ITS) to help organisations manage computing resources more efficiently.
The capability dynamically adjusts compute usage according to the complexity of a query, allowing organisations to allocate more resources when more complex reasoning is required and reduce usage for simpler requests.
The release also includes CPU offloading for more efficient GPU memory management, with storage offloading available as a developer preview.
These capabilities are designed to allow models to handle longer conversations and larger documents without necessarily requiring additional GPU hardware.
Red Hat AI 3.5 also supports multimodal serving through vLLM Omni in early access, allowing text, audio and image generation to be served through a unified serving layer.
The latest release extends distributed inference capabilities beyond OpenShift to third-party Kubernetes services.
Red Hat said this provides a more consistent model-serving experience across cloud environments, with the technology now generally available on CoreWeave CKS and Microsoft Azure, while Amazon EKS is available as a technology preview.
The platform also expands GPU-as-a-Service and multi-tenancy capabilities, including namespace isolation, hosted control plane support and real-time dashboard visibility into hardware inventories, active utilisation and dynamic GPU capacity borrowing.
For enterprises operating AI across complex infrastructure environments, these capabilities are intended to provide greater consistency and control.
Joe Fernandes, Vice President and General Manager of the AI Business Unit at Red Hat, said the conversation around enterprise AI has moved beyond simply putting AI into production.
“The conversation has moved from getting AI into production to running it at scale as trusted enterprise infrastructure, which requires safety evidence, governed agents, cost attribution and multi-tenancy,” he said.
Fernandes said Red Hat AI 3.5 provides the operational controls, verifiable trust and agentic foundations needed to run AI as a safe and accountable enterprise architecture across hybrid cloud environments.
By bringing AI safety evaluation, observability, multi-tenancy, agent development and resource controls into a unified platform, Red Hat aims to help organisations transition from isolated AI experiments towards governed AI services that can operate across the enterprise.
Red Hat AI 3.5 is now generally available and is also available as part of Red Hat AI Factory with NVIDIA.
The release represents Red Hat’s latest effort to give enterprises the infrastructure and governance capabilities needed to scale AI while maintaining visibility over safety, performance, resource utilisation and operational control.

title: Volvo Car Malaysia Launches EX30 Cross Country for Electric Adventures Beyond the City
bodyText:
From weekday office commutes to weekend glamping trips, Volvo Car Malaysia is positioning its latest electric SUV as a vehicle designed to bridge urban mobility and outdoor exploration.
The company has unveiled the new Volvo EX30 Cross Country, Volvo’s first fully electric Cross Country model, designed for tailpipe emission-free journeys while offering additional capability for rougher road conditions.
Priced from RM218,888, the locally assembled EX30 Cross Country is now available for viewing at authorised Volvo dealers nationwide. Early adopters can also access a limited-time launch package for the first 100 reservations.
Chris Wailes, Managing Director of Volvo Cars Malaysia and Thailand, said Malaysia’s combination of urban environments and natural landscapes makes it an ideal setting for the EX30 Cross Country.
“The adage that ‘life is full of adventures’ is so apt when we describe living in Malaysia because it is a country where you can find some of the oldest rainforests in the region just a few hours away from the tallest building in the world.”
He said the EX30 Cross Country was designed to offer the freedom to explore while providing confidence across different environments.
Volvo’s Cross Country heritage dates back to 1997, when the first Cross Country model was introduced to handle the demanding Scandinavian climate.
Since then, Volvo said its Cross Country vehicles have been tested and refined across a variety of road conditions, including wet surfaces, rough terrain, highways and muddy tracks.
The EX30 Cross Country builds on the award-winning EX30 while adding features intended to make it more capable beyond urban roads.
As Volvo’s first fully electric Cross Country model, it combines zero tailpipe emissions with a more rugged design and enhanced chassis characteristics for drivers looking to venture beyond the city.
As a compact SUV, the EX30 Cross Country is designed for urban environments such as the Klang Valley. Its 360-degree environmental awareness system uses radars positioned at each corner alongside multiple sensors to assist drivers when navigating expressways and tighter roads.
The electric SUV offers a driving range of up to 437km, while its 69kWh NMC battery can be charged from 10% to 80% in around 27 minutes using a 175kW DC rapid charger.
For more demanding journeys, the EX30 Cross Country is equipped with a twin-motor all-wheel-drive system producing 428hp and 543Nm of torque. It can accelerate from 0 to 100km/h in 3.7 seconds.
Fine-tuned steering software is also designed to optimise steering torque build-up, active return and damping, providing greater control through tight corners and a stronger connection to the road.
The model has 19mm more ground clearance than the standard EX30. Combined with its advanced chassis design and 19-inch five-spoke wheels, this is intended to improve comfort and stability when travelling over more challenging surfaces.
The EX30 Cross Country builds on the EX30’s positioning as Volvo’s most sustainable car to date.
As a fully electric vehicle, it produces zero tailpipe emissions, while its interior incorporates materials such as upcycled denim textiles and bio-attributed Nordico upholstery.
Safety remains central to the model, with Volvo’s latest Safe Space Technology and advanced driver assistance systems designed to protect occupants and those around the vehicle.
The system includes braking and steering support for collision avoidance, a Driver Understanding system, as well as next-generation Pilot Assist and Park Pilot Assist.
The EX30 Cross Country retains the minimalist Scandinavian design language of the standard EX30 while introducing additional rugged detailing.
Matt black and vapour grey accents are paired with low-gloss vapour grey skid plates, matte black lower bumpers and wheel arch extensions.
A Cross Country nameplate on the C-pillar, embossed CC logo at the rear and low-gloss rear shield design further distinguish the model.
Inside, the cabin draws inspiration from the deep blue and indigo tones of a starry night sky, alongside purple hues reminiscent of a sunset.
The interior features charcoal-coloured woven textile, Nordico upholstery, denim decor panels and blue air vent panels. A panoramic roof allows natural light into the cabin while providing occupants with a wider view of their surroundings.
The EX30 Cross Country comes with built-in Google Services, including Google Assistant, Google Maps and access to apps through the Google Play Store via its 12.3-inch centre screen.
An advanced Harman Kardon Premium Sound system is paired with wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto connectivity.
Practicality is also a key feature, with the model retaining the EX30’s smart storage solutions. Large door compartments replace conventional door-mounted speakers, which have been relocated to a dashboard soundbar.
A flexible central storage area between the driver and passenger can accommodate a handbag, while a removable rear box beneath the central armrest provides additional storage and doubles as a waste bin.
The rear luggage compartment provides 318 litres of space with all seats in place, increasing to 718 litres when the second-row split seats are fully folded.
A ‘Will it Fit’ graphic on the power tailgate provides examples of items that can be transported, while optional accessories include mud flaps, load carriers, bicycle racks and a roof basket.
The locally assembled Volvo EX30 Cross Country is available in Crystal White, Vapour Grey and Cloud Blue, with prices starting from RM218,888 without insurance.
For the first 100 reservations, Volvo Car Malaysia is offering a launch package comprising a RM12,000 cash rebate, a complimentary Volvo Wallbox worth RM3,990, a Load Carrier worth RM2,098 and a Roof Basket worth RM3,680.
Key specifications include:
Alongside the Cross Country launch, Volvo Car Malaysia has also announced updates to the EX30 Ultra.
The model is now available from RM198,888 without insurance, broadening the accessibility of Volvo’s electric vehicle line-up in Malaysia.
The EX30 Ultra is offered in four exterior colours: Crystal White, Vapour Grey, Cloud Blue and Onyx Black.
The launch of the EX30 Cross Country also marks the introduction of Digital Service Booking (DSB) by Volvo Car Malaysia.
The new platform allows customers to schedule aftersales service appointments through the Volvo Car Malaysia website or the Volvo Cars App, providing greater flexibility and convenience for vehicle servicing.
DSB is currently available through Volvo authorised retailers in the Klang Valley, with plans to expand the service to authorised retailers in other regions across Malaysia.
With the EX30 Cross Country, Volvo Car Malaysia is combining its established Cross Country heritage with electric mobility, offering Malaysian drivers an SUV designed to move between urban roads and outdoor adventures without tailpipe emissions.

title: MRCA Calls for Budget 2027 Measures to Build a Sustainable and Competitive Retail Sector
bodyText:
As Malaysia prepares for the tabling of Budget 2027 by Prime Minister and Finance Minister YAB Dato’ Seri Anwar Ibrahim on 9 October 2026, the Malaysia Retail Chain Association (MRCA) has outlined a strategic fiscal wishlist aimed at fostering a sustainable, competitive and resilient retail sector.
Malaysian businesses are navigating an increasingly complex operating environment, with rising operational costs and growing competition from overseas players. Against this backdrop, MRCA said policy consistency, regulatory clarity and equitable economic frameworks are essential to improving productivity and supporting job creation.
The association has called on the Ministry of Finance to consider several macroeconomic measures when formulating Budget 2027, with its proposals centred on creating a fairer operating environment for local retailers while supporting long-term economic growth.
One of MRCA’s key concerns is the compliance disparity between local brick-and-mortar retailers and foreign e-commerce platforms offering ultra-low-priced goods to Malaysian consumers.
The association said local retailers continue to face significant compliance obligations while some cross-border platforms remain untaxed or under-taxed. According to MRCA, this structural imbalance places pressure on domestic businesses and could contribute to erosion of the national tax base.
To address the issue, MRCA is calling for stricter policies and more equitable surcharges on cross-border e-commerce transactions, including stronger enforcement of the Sales Tax on Low-Value Goods (LVG).
The association is also urging the Government to strengthen regulatory controls against counterfeit and inferior goods sold through e-commerce platforms.
Such measures, MRCA said, would help protect consumer safety and quality standards while safeguarding the intellectual property and interests of legitimate brand owners.
MRCA has also highlighted the rising tax burden on commercial operations, particularly where businesses are required to pay taxes on costs that are effectively operational reimbursements.
One immediate concern is the 6% Service Tax on utility supplies for commercial tenants paying through mall management, which took effect on 1 July 2026.
The association is calling for an exemption from the Service Tax on these utility pass-through payments, arguing that taxing such reimbursements creates an inequitable double-taxation effect and contributes to higher operating costs for businesses.
MRCA is also proposing targeted tax rebates or double tax deductions for commercial stakeholders investing in ESG-related operational upgrades.
In particular, the association wants incentives for investments in facility governance, public safety, active fire safety systems and modernised infrastructure. Such incentives could encourage businesses to make capital investments that improve both operational resilience and public safety.
The association is further maintaining its proposal to reduce the Service Tax on construction and renovation services to 3%, noting that building materials are already subject to taxation.
Another major proposal in MRCA’s Budget 2027 wishlist is the phased reintroduction of the Goods and Services Tax (GST).
